title: The Joyful Morn, My God, Is Come
description: The Joyful Morn, My God, Is Come in Tonic Solfa to MERIBAH, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 62 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Sabbath and the Earthly Temple”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MERIBAH; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The joy-ful morn, my God, is come, That calls me to thy sa-cred dome, Thy pre-sence to a-dore: My feet the sum-mons shall at-tend, With will-ing steps thy courts as-cend And tread the hal-lowed floor.

lines: The joyful morn, my God, is come,
That calls me to thy sacred dome,
My feet the summons shall attend,
With willing steps thy courts ascend
With holy joy I hail the day,
That warns my thirsting soul away;
For, lo! my great Redeemer's power
And leads me to his rest!
Lo! the redeemed of God ascend,
In hymns of praise their tongues employ,

licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MERIBAH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
